text:
Lucas: FYI - customer Acme hit a streaming decode failure that only shows up when their client retries mid-stream. They see truncated JSON + a scanner hang and end up getting double-billed for the same request id. Repro steps below.

Maya: ugh. Can you paste the minimal repro and their SDK + Go version? Also any example logs?

Lucas: steps to repro (works locally for me):
```bash
# simulate chunked streaming with small TCP chunks
curl -v -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer redwood-test' \
  --http1.1 \
  --no-buffer \
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=gpt-test' \
  --data-binary @payload.json
```
Logs we see on client:
```
decoder error: unexpected EOF while reading object
stream: scanner stopped, no final newline
retrying request (id=abc-123)\n...server accepts retry and charges again
```
And a tiny Go client that triggers it (uses bufio.Scanner):
```go
package main
import (
  "bufio"
  "fmt"
  "net/http"
  "os"
)
func main() {
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=gpt-test", nil)
  req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer redwood-test")
  resp, _ := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
  scanner := bufio.NewScanner(resp.Body)
  for scanner.Scan() {
    line := scanner.Text()
    fmt.Println("chunk:", line)
  }
  if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {
    fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "scanner err:", err)
  }
}
```
Note: SDK version they run is go-redwood v0.9.4, go1.20. They also have an aggressive client retry layer that retries on any network error.

Charlie: Does the service send NDJSON / newline framing? If chunk boundary splits a JSON object mid-object bufio.Scanner will wait for a newline and can hit token size or EOF.

Lucas: Right — server streams newline-delimited JSON events, but in their failure case the client TCP connection is torn (FIN) while a JSON object is partially streamed. Our runtime currently flushes the final token without an explicit boundary marker; client sees EOF mid-object. Their retry layer interprets that as a failed request and re-sends -> duplicate billing.

Maya: Can you capture the raw bytes on the wire (tcpdump) to confirm whether the server sent a final `\n` or not? If it's server-side missing final newline we can push a runtime fix to always append a boundary marker on the last chunk.

Lucas: I have a tcpdump snippet showing the last bytes are "..., \"text\":\"hello\"}" then connection close — no trailing newline. Attaching excerpt.

Tony: For immediate workaround customers can: 1) avoid bufio.Scanner (it requires newline framing) and use a streaming json.Decoder that tolerates EOF on partial objects, or 2) set retry classifier to treat truncated/EOF as non-retry (so billing isn't duplicated).

Maya: Agreed. Also file a runtime bug — we should: a) ensure last chunk includes a single separator token ("\n\n" or "\n--END--\n") and b) add an optional per-stream ack header so clients can know finality before charging.

Lucas: I've raised a support ticket with engineering (ENG-8243) and attached tcpdump + small repro. For the customer I recommended switching their Go snippet to use json.Decoder:
```go
dec := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body)
for {
  var ev map[string]interface{}
  if err := dec.Decode(&ev); err != nil {
    if err == io.EOF {
      // treat as end-of-stream, don't auto-retry
      break
    }
    // handle malformed partial object
    log.Println("decode err", err)
    break
  }
  // process ev
}
```

Charlie: Pull request idea for runtime: ensure when we close a streaming response we append a single 0x0a byte if last sent chunk doesn't end with \n. Low risk. Also add a unit test that closes mid-object to reproduce.

infra-bot: deploy job queued for branch fix/stream-framing-marker (ci#4521).

billing-bot: note: account Acme (acct-554) refunded duplicate charge, created case BILL-993.

Maya: Thanks everyone. Action items: Lucas — send customer the json.Decoder workaround & confirm SDK version pinned; Charlie — PR for trailing-frame marker + test; Tony — update retry classifier docs with guidance about truncated-stream vs hard network errors. We'll follow up in ENG-8243. :thumbsup:

Lucas: Will do, updating ticket with customer acceptance.
